passage: Zubin, my classmate at college, asked if he could join our Ganesh aarti, and I was curious how it would go. He arrived on time, left his shoes at the door and stood at the back with his hands loosely together, watching. He asked my mother quietly whether it was fine to take a photo of the idol. She said there was no need, and he nodded. When the aarti ended he took the prasad in his right hand, said thank you and asked what the modak stood for. My mother explained. He listened, asked one more question and told us about the fire temple where his family goes for Navroz. I can't say what he felt inside, but he looked interested, not pretending. At the door he said, "Thank you for letting me see it." Shreya

qa.q: What did Zubin ask after the aarti ended?
qa.a: Zubin asked what the modak stood for.

qa.q: What does Zubin's behaviour suggest he feels, and how sure can Shreya be?
qa.a: He seems interested and respectful, but Shreya cannot be certain of his inner state. Shreya only reads it from how he asked and listened.

qa.q: Which choices by Zubin showed respectful curiosity?
qa.a: He arrived on time, left his shoes at the door, stood at the back, asked before taking a photo, thanked the family and asked questions without pretending belief.

qa.q: How might Shreya's mother have felt answering Zubin's questions?
qa.a: Probably welcoming and glad to explain, since she answered patiently and told him there was no need for a photo.

grounding: A young adult attends a friend's family prayer to learn, asking respectfully and following local etiquette without any wish to change belief.

passage: Saturday. Avni asked her friend Asif, "Could I come to your family's iftar next week and watch the evening prayer? I want to learn, not to join." Asif smiled. "Ask Ammi, she'll be happy. Bring a dupatta for your head and leave your shoes outside." Wednesday. At Asif's home the family laid out the prayer mats. Avni sat quietly on a chair by the wall, head covered, and took no photos. Afterwards she asked Asif's mother, "Would it be all right to ask what you say?" and listened carefully to the answer. She ate dates and did not pretend to pray. Friday. Avni texted Asif: "Thank you. I felt welcome. I'm still myself, but I understand a little more."

qa.q: On which day did Avni ask Asif about the iftar?
How does Avni seem to feel by Friday?
qa.a: Avni feels welcome and grateful. Avni thanks Asif and says, "I'm still myself, but I understand a little more."

qa.q: Which choice by Avni at Asif's home showed respect without pretending?
qa.a: She sat quietly with her head covered, took no photos, asked politely what was said, and did not pretend to pray.

qa.q: How might Asif's mother have felt when Avni asked what she says?
qa.a: Probably pleased and respected, since Avni asked politely and listened carefully to the answer.

grounding: A young adult attends a friend's family prayer to learn, asking respectfully and following etiquette without any wish to change belief.
